message_source_quote: Calibrated the pipeline by exactly reproducing the white-bear (WBS, Raman 2026) vector — its ‖d‖ matched the paper's Table A1 to 3 decimals — which gave 0.686 at `prefix` (their 0.44 read-cell-only figure reproduced too), establishing the dose/position geometry.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that the white-bear contrast - holding versus thought-suppression of an instructed concept - steers this readout, and explicitly left the bench's secret and preference conditions untested.

differences.message_quote: Calibrated the pipeline by exactly reproducing the white-bear (WBS, Raman 2026) vector — its ‖d‖ matched the paper's Table A1 to 3 decimals — which gave 0.686 at `prefix` (their 0.44 read-cell-only figure reproduced too), establishing the dose/position geometry.
differences.writeup_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that the white-bear contrast - holding versus thought-suppression of an instructed concept - steers this readout, and explicitly left the bench's secret and preference conditions untested.

rationale: Both documents credit Raman et al. (2026) / the white-bear steering paper as the direct basis for the method, framing preference-concealment as a novel contrast variant that the source explicitly left untested, and both report the same fit-split numbers and one-sided null. The message additionally discloses a concrete calibration step - exactly reproducing the source's white-bear vector and matching its Table A1 figures to three decimals - that the write-up never mentions, so the message gives a more detailed and quantified picture of how closely the work reproduces/builds on the source before diverging.
